checks: After identifying aff F isometrically with R^m and translating x_0, the input is a full-dimensional convex m-body with an interior mark. The accepted minimizer has denominator strictly positive on the whole compact body, and its first moment identity uses exactly the density L^(−m−2).

The chart inverse is y/(1−a·y) after the translation. Positive endpoint denominators give the full image of a segment by positive reweighting. The Jacobian is L^(−m−1), so the image volume is E, its first moment is the stationary integral, and dividing the escort density by this Jacobian yields ell(y)/E.

The graph height ell is affine and strictly positive on the compact image D. Its subgraph has nonempty (m+1)-interior and volume E by the volume and centroid identities. Fubini shows that the normalized uniform volume projects to the normalized escort. The lifted centroid projects to a point in D.

A physical closed halfspace with intrinsic margin u·(x−x_0)≥b pulls back to (u+ba)·y≥b since ell>0. If the transformed margin is constant and contains the selected point it contains all of D. Otherwise ordinary Grünbaum applies to the lifted containing halfspace and gives Γ_{m+1}, including at boundary. The singleton and codimension statements follow directly.

For the interval objective the denominator product (1−at)(1+a(1−t)) is a strictly concave quadratic, maximized at a=(1−2t)/(2t(1−t)). The endpoint denominator values are 1/[2(1−t)] and 1/(2t), giving E=4t(1−t). The upper integral from t is [1−(2t)^2]/(2aE)=1/4+t/2 for a≠0, and at a=0 the uniform computation gives 1/2. Complementation gives the lower integral. Exact fraction spot checks agree.
